WHAT IS THE ISSUE:
- Root cause: Wire feed motor overload caused by improper wire tension (measured 18 kg vs expected 22 kg) after a new wire spool and recent drive-roll replacement, leading to excessive load on motor. Evidence: expert fix (G. Phani) and alarm pattern linking overloads to spool/roll changes.
- Difference from historical pattern: First occurrence of three consecutive overload alarms in a single shift; prior events were isolated single alarms.

WHAT IS THE IMPACT:
- Production impact: Line stopped; estimated downtime ~1 hour.
- Safety risk: LOW (no electrical, fire, or gas breach reported); however, parts welded during the fault must be quarantined per critical warnings.
- Financial impact: Lost production time (~1 hour) plus potential scrap of parts welded during the fault event.

HOW CRITICAL IS IT:
- HIGH
- Justification: Three overload alarms occurred in one shift and production was stopped per SOP, meeting the HIGH minimum criteria.

HOW TO ADDRESS IT:
- Immediate action:
  Step 1: Safety - Isolate power at the main disconnect and apply LOTO before any inspection or repair.
  Step 2: Diagnosis - Verify current wire tension; inspect drive rolls for wear; inspect wire liner for blockage; confirm shielding gas is present and flow is correct.
  Step 3: Fix - 
    • Option A (expert fix): Open the tension dial cover, reset tension from 18 to 22, then run a test weld. (G. Phani, 2026-07-28) 
    • Option B (knowledge-graph warning): Do NOT continue adjusting tension; instead replace/inspect drive rolls and liner as per WI-WM101-001. 
    • Note: Contradiction - expert fix recommends tension adjustment while the knowledge graph flags tension adjustment as the WRONG RESPONSE. Engineering review required before proceeding with either option.
  Step 4: Verify - Perform a test weld, monitor for overload alarms, check arc voltage (target 15.5 V) and ensure no further alarms for at least 5 minutes.
  Step 5: Quality - Quarantine any parts welded during the fault event for inspection; scrap any welds performed without shielding gas.
  Additional mandatory actions:
    • If liner replacement is performed, complete burn-in procedure: run wire at 5.0 m/min for 30 seconds; wire instability during burn-in is EXPECTED and not a new fault.
    • Do NOT keep adjusting tension beyond the initial correction; repeated adjustments risk motor burnout (per knowledge graph warning).

- Root cause fix (permanent solution):
  • Implement a mandatory wire-tension verification step after every new spool installation and after any linear or drive-roll replacement.
  • Update SOP to include the verified tension value (22 kg) and to prohibit further tension adjustments as a troubleshooting method.

WHAT IS THE ISSUE:
- Root cause: Improper or blocked wire liner after replacement causing feed stutter; evidence from SOP (manual pull test) and knowledge-graph root-cause "Wire Liner Blocked → Fixed by Liner and Drive Roll Replacement".
- Difference from historical pattern: No overload alarm triggered; stutter appears immediately after liner change; historical alarm was overload requiring tension release and drive-roll adjustment.

WHAT IS THE IMPACT:
- Production impact: Line operating with degraded weld quality; estimated downtime ~1 hour to correct.
- Safety risk: MEDIUM - risk of motor burnout if tension is repeatedly adjusted; LOTO required for safe maintenance.
- Financial impact: Approximate loss of one hour of production plus potential scrap of parts welded during fault (per knowledge-graph "Parts welded after alarm must be scrapped").

HOW CRITICAL IS IT:
- HIGH - maintenance will require LOTO and a production stop; recurring fault indicator (new liner causing issue) meets criticality rule for faults requiring isolation.

HOW TO ADDRESS IT:
- Immediate action:
  Step 1: Safety - Isolate power at main disconnect (LOTO) before any work on WM-101.
  Step 2: Diagnosis - Stop welding, manually pull wire through liner and note resistance; if resistance is high, liner is blocked.
  Step 3: Fix - Remove and reinstall liner according to WI-WM101-001; ensure proper seating and clearance; do NOT adjust tension further (per NCR-2024-047).
  Step 4: Burn-in - Complete burn-in procedure: run wire at 5.0 m/min for 30 seconds; note that instability during this period is EXPECTED and not a new fault.
  Step 5: Verify - Observe feed for steady operation within 4.5-6.0 m/min; perform test weld; confirm arc voltage returns to normal range (15-16 V) and no stutter.
  Step 6: Quality - Quarantine any parts welded during the fault event for inspection; scrap if alarm condition later confirmed.
- Root cause fix (permanent solution): Implement a post-replacement checklist that includes resistance check, proper liner seating verification, and mandatory burn-in before returning to production.
- Preventive action: Train operators on the "Do NOT adjust tension" rule; update work instruction to require documented burn-in sign-off; schedule periodic audit of liner replacements.
- Who to notify: Maintenance Supervisor, Production Manager, Quality Assurance Lead.

WHAT IS THE ISSUE:
- Root cause: Shielding gas pressure was low, likely due to a cylinder, regulator, or hose problem, causing inadequate shielding and pitted welds (expert fix + knowledge-graph root cause).
- What is different: This is the first documented WM-101 low-pressure alarm; no historical pattern exists.

WHAT IS THE IMPACT:
- Production impact: Line stopped for ~1 hour; parts welded during the alarm window must be quarantined and are likely to be scrapped.
- Safety risk: CRITICAL - welding without shielding gas is prohibited and creates fire/fume hazards.
- Financial impact: Cost of scrapped parts plus 1 hour downtime; exact amount not quantified.

HOW CRITICAL IS IT:
- CRITICAL - alarm forced production stop, safety warning is critical, and LOTO is required before any maintenance.

HOW TO ADDRESS IT:
- Immediate action
  Step 1: Safety - Apply LOTO, isolate power at the main disconnect before any work.
  Step 2: Diagnosis - Inspect gas cylinder pressure, regulator setting, and hose for leaks; confirm pressure meets equipment spec.
  Step 3: Fix - Increase gas flow to the proper setpoint; refill or replace the cylinder and repair/replace regulator or hose as needed.
  Step 4: Verify - Re-trigger the alarm test to confirm pressure is within tolerance; perform a test weld and inspect for proper shielding.
  Step 5: Quality - Quarantine all parts welded during the low-pressure window; inspect and scrap any that fail quality criteria.
  Additional mandatory actions:
  - Do NOT keep adjusting tension - this will not fix the gas issue and risks motor burnout (cited NCR-2024-047).
  - If liner replacement is required, complete burn-in procedure after replacement: run wire at 5.0 m/min for 30 seconds; wire instability during burn-in is expected, not a new fault.

- Root cause fix (permanent solution)
  - Implement scheduled inspections and pressure verification of gas cylinders, regulators, and hoses; replace components before pressure drops below threshold; update SOP to include pre-run gas pressure check.

- Preventive action
  - Add gas-pressure check to the shift-start checklist; train operators to verify shielding-gas flow before welding; record pressure readings in the shift report.

- Who to notify
  - Maintenance Supervisor, Production Control, Quality Assurance, Safety Officer.
